# `silk/text/glob`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Glob patterns: compile a pattern such as `src/**/*.{silk,toml}` and test paths against it,
and inspect text for glob syntax.

## When to use
Use [`Pattern`](#Pattern) to select files by name, for example to filter a directory listing or a list
of changed paths. To find matching files on a file system, use `silk.system.glob_scan`, which
walks directories with this matcher.

## Details
A pattern is a list of segments separated by `/`:

- `*` matches any characters within one segment, and `?` matches one character that is not a
  separator.
- `**` as a whole segment matches any number of segments, including none, so `a/**/b` matches
  `a/b` and `a/x/y/b`.
- `[abc]`, `[a-z]`, `[!abc]` and `[^abc]` match one character from, or not from, a set. A class
  can name `/` explicitly. POSIX named classes such as `[:alpha:]` are not expanded.
- `{a,b}` matches one of its alternatives, which can nest. `{1..9}`, `{01..10}`, `{9..1..2}` and
  `{a..g}` match one value of a numeric or letter range, with padding and a step.
- `?(a|b)`, `*(a|b)`, `+(a|b)`, `@(a|b)` and `!(a|b)` match zero or one, any number, one or
  more, exactly one, or none of the alternatives.
- A leading `!` inverts the result, and `\` escapes the next character.

An unclosed class, brace or group, and a bare parenthesis, are literal text. The rules and the
test expectations follow the `picomatch` package; [`isGlob`](#isGlob) and [`globParent`](#globParent) follow
`is-glob` and `glob-parent`.

Patterns and paths are text. [`Pattern`](#Pattern) and the inspection functions also have `Bytes` forms
for host patterns and paths that are not UTF-8. Matching never normalizes a path.

## Examples
### Test paths against one compiled pattern
```silk
import silk.text.glob { Pattern, Dots }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }

effect fn check() -> i32 ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let sources = run Pattern.make("src/**/*.{silk,toml}")
  let nested = run Pattern.matches(&sources, "src/driver/main.silk", Dots.Match)
  let other = run Pattern.matches(&sources, "docs/index.md", Dots.Match)
  let hidden = run Pattern.matches(&sources, "src/.cache/x.silk", Dots.Hide)
  if !nested.matches || other.matches || hidden.matches {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}

effect fn exhausted(error: OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  drop error
  return 2
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  return run Effect.catchAll(check(), exhausted) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
}
```

Import as `glob` with `import silk.text.glob as glob`.

<a id="Dots"></a>

## `Dots`

```silk
pub enum Dots
```

How wildcards treat path segments that start with `.`.

### Details

Only wildcards (`*`, `?`, `**`, classes and groups) are restricted. A pattern that spells a
leading `.` literally, such as `.github/*`, matches such segments in every mode.

<a id="Dots.Match"></a>

### `Match`

```silk
Match
```

Wildcards match every segment, including hidden names and `.` and `..`.

<a id="Dots.SkipTraversal"></a>

### `SkipTraversal`

```silk
SkipTraversal
```

Wildcards do not match the segments `.` and `..`, but do match other hidden names.

<a id="Dots.Hide"></a>

### `Hide`

```silk
Hide
```

Wildcards match no segment that starts with `.`, so `.` and `..` are excluded too.

<a id="Separators"></a>

## `Separators`

```silk
pub enum Separators
```

Which bytes of a candidate path separate its segments.

<a id="Separators.Slash"></a>

### `Slash`

```silk
Slash
```

Only `/` separates segments, as on POSIX hosts.

<a id="Separators.SlashOrBackslash"></a>

### `SlashOrBackslash`

```silk
SlashOrBackslash
```

Both `/` and `\` separate segments, as in Windows paths. The pattern itself still uses
`/` between segments and `\` as its escape.

<a id="Pattern"></a>

## `Pattern`

```silk
pub struct Pattern
```

A compiled glob pattern that can be matched against many paths.

### When to use

Compile a pattern once with [`Pattern.make`](#Pattern.impl.make) and match it with [`Pattern.matches`](#Pattern.impl.matches) when you
test more than one path. For a single test, [`matches`](#Pattern.impl.matches) compiles and matches in one call.

### Details

A `Pattern` owns a copy of its source and its compiled program, so the source can be dropped
after [`Pattern.make`](#Pattern.impl.make) returns. Matching runs in time proportional to the pattern size times
the path length: groups and braces are compiled into one program, never expanded into every
alternative.

```silk
    ! OutOfMemoryError
```

Compiles `pattern`.

#### Details

Every pattern compiles. An unclosed class, brace or group is matched as literal text, as
is a bare parenthesis.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the compiled program.

```silk
    ! OutOfMemoryError

```

Compiles the pattern `pattern`, given as host bytes that need not be UTF-8.

#### Details

Bytes that are not UTF-8 match themselves. `?` and classes consume one Unicode scalar of
the candidate.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the compiled program.

<a id="Pattern.impl.matches"></a>

### Method `matches`

```silk
pub effect fn matches(self: &Self, path: string, dots: Dots) -> MatchResult
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Matches `path` against the pattern, with `/` as the only separator.

#### Details

The path is matched as written: it is not normalized, so `a/./b` and `a/b` are different
paths. `dots` decides whether wildcards match hidden segments.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the scratch rows, which are
  proportional to the pattern size.

```silk
    ! OutOfMemoryError

```

Matches the host path `path`, which need not be UTF-8, with `/` as the only separator.

#### Details

A byte that is not part of valid UTF-8 counts as one character for `?` and classes.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the scratch rows.

against a pattern written with `/`.

<a id="matches"></a>

## `matches`

```silk
pub effect fn matches(pattern: string, path: string) -> MatchResult
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Compiles `pattern` and matches `path` against it once, with `Dots.Match` and `/` as the only
separator.

### When to use

Use it for a single test. To test many paths, compile once with [`Pattern.make`](#Pattern.impl.make).

### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the compiled program or scratch rows.

```silk
pub fn isGlobBytes(text: &[u8]) -> bool
```

Whether the host bytes `text` are a glob pattern by the rules of the `is-glob` package,

<a id="globParentBytes"></a>

## `globParentBytes`

```silk
pub effect fn globParentBytes(pattern: &[u8]) -> Bytes
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the longest leading directory of the host bytes `pattern` that contains no glob
syntax, with escapes removed, by the rules of the `glob-parent` package, version 6.0.2.

### Details

A pattern with no literal directory gives `.`. It looks only at the bytes, never at a file
system, and keeps bytes that are not glob syntax as they are, also when they are not UTF-8.

### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the result.

<a id="isGlob"></a>

## `isGlob`

```silk
pub fn isGlob(text: string) -> bool
```

Whether `text` is a glob pattern by the rules of the `is-glob` package, version 4.0.3.

### When to use

Use it to decide whether a user-written path should be matched as a pattern or used as
written. An unclosed `[` or `{` does not count, and neither does an escaped character.

<a id="hasExtglobPrefix"></a>

## `hasExtglobPrefix`

```silk
pub fn hasExtglobPrefix(text: string) -> bool
```

Whether `text` contains an unescaped `@(`, `+(` or `!(`, whether or not it is closed.

<a id="detectGlobSyntax"></a>

## `detectGlobSyntax`

```silk
pub fn detectGlobSyntax(text: string) -> bool
```

Whether `text` contains any unescaped glob syntax: `*`, `?`, `[`, `{`, a leading `!` or an
extglob prefix, even when a group is never closed.

### When to use

Use it to find text that a glob matcher would treat differently from a literal path. It is
broader than [`isGlob`](#isGlob), which also requires groups to be closed.

<a id="globParent"></a>

## `globParent`

```silk
pub effect fn globParent(pattern: string) -> String
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the longest leading directory of `pattern` that contains no glob syntax, with escapes
removed, by the rules of the `glob-parent` package, version 6.0.2.

### When to use

Use it to find the directory a scan for `pattern` must start from: `src/**/*.silk` gives
`src`, and a pattern with no literal directory gives `.`.

### Details

It looks only at the text and never at a file system. Segments are separated by `/`.

### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the result.
